problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: F may be nonconvex. It has a global lower bound a with F(x₀) − a ≤ Δ, where Δ ≥ 0 and L > 0. A minimizer need not exist.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is the uniform average F(x) = (1/n) Σᵢ fᵢ(x) of n ≥ 1 differentiable worker objectives. The L-Lipschitz gradient condition applies to F. Component gradients may vary arbitrarily across workers.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A completed evaluation at worker i returns the query point x and a jointly measurable local gradient estimate gᵢ(x,ξ) with mean ∇fᵢ(x). Each completion uses the next sample in that worker’s stream.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, system and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation.answer.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A timed communication oracle carries finite bit strings between a central node and each worker. An m-bit payload takes l + b(m + 64) time. Each directed link permits one outstanding message, and distinct links can operate concurrently. Worker i can have one evaluation pending, with completion time hᵢ > 0 unless aborted. The central node has no gradient oracle.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation, communication and system. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, clockBits and step. LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, system and spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every i and x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σᵢ², with σᵢ ≥ 0. Samples are IID within worker i with law μᵢ. The entire sample streams are independent across workers, whose marginal laws may differ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries and outputs belong to Euclidean ℝᵈ with its ℓ₂ norm, where d is a public natural number.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The algorithm knows d, n, x₀, L, Δ, ε, every hᵢ and σᵢ, the latency l ≥ 0, the time per bit b ≥ 0, and the measurable sample space. The component functions, stochastic gradient maps and sample laws belong to the hidden instance and oracle.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance and spec.admissible. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output X is a measurable point read from the algorithm’s designated root at the prescribed deadline. The stationarity criterion uses the first power of the aggregate gradient norm, E‖∇F(X)‖ ≤ ε, with ε > 0.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Output, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gradient norm must be integrable under the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds. The accuracy bound is in expectation at a fixed elapsed-time budget. Execution must also have finitely many events almost surely up to that deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedAggregateSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The benchmark couples smoothness of the aggregate objective with worker-specific sampling times and variances. Its fixed deadline charges latency and every transmitted bit on concurrent directed star links.
